Desirability Score Table of the BOIN12 Design

Source: R/boin12_decision_table.R
boin12_decision_table.Rd

Tabulate the desirability of a dose for every possible outcome of the patients treated there, as in Table 3 of Lin et al. (2020): the posterior probability that the utility of the dose exceeds the benchmark, its rank-based desirability score (RDS) and whether the dose is admissible.

Usage

boin12_decision_table(
  target,
  target_resp,
  n = c(0, 3, 6, 9),
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.9,
  psi00 = 40,
  psi11 = 60,
  benchmark_weight = 0.5,
  utility_prior = c(1, 1)
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Highest acceptable DLT probability, called phi_T by Lin et al. (2020). It is the target of the BOIN boundaries lambda_e and lambda_d, of the admissibility of a dose and of the MTD that bounds the OBD. Lin et al. recommend a value slightly above the target of a design that only considers toxicity, for example 0.35 instead of 0.30.

target_resp

Numeric scalar. Lowest acceptable response probability, phi_E. Note that this is a lower limit, as in sim_bf_boin_et, whereas the target_resp of sim_boin_et is a target.

n

Integer vector. Numbers of patients at a dose to tabulate. Defaults to c(0, 3, 6, 9).

p_saf, p_tox

Numeric scalars or NULL. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic and lowest deemed overly toxic, which give the BOIN boundaries. Default to 0.6 * target and 1.4 * target.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A dose is inadmissible, together with every higher dose, when the posterior probability that its DLT rate exceeds target is at least this cutoff. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. A dose is inadmissible when the posterior probability that its response rate is below target_resp is at least this cutoff. Defaults to 0.90.

psi00, psi11

Numeric scalars from 0 to 100. Utility of a patient without DLT and without response, and with both. The utility of a response without DLT is 100 and that of a DLT without response is 0. Default to 40 and 60, the example of Lin et al. (2020).

benchmark_weight

Numeric scalar above 0 and at most 1. The utility benchmark is benchmark_weight * u_low + (1 - benchmark_weight) * 100, where u_low is the expected utility of a dose whose DLT and response probabilities are target and target_resp, the two outcomes being independent. Defaults to 0.5, the benchmark of Lin et al. (2020); Lu et al. (2025) use 0.6.

utility_prior

Numeric vector of two positive numbers. Beta prior of the utility of a dose divided by 100. Defaults to c(1, 1).

Value

A data frame of class boin12_decision_table with one row per outcome and columns n, n_tox, n_resp, n_tox_resp (patients with both a DLT and a response; only when psi00 + psi11 is not 100, since the utility otherwise depends on the margins alone), admissible, desirability and score. The design parameters are kept in the attribute "design", a list with lambda_e, lambda_d, u_low and u_benchmark among others.

Details

The utility of a patient is 100 for a response without DLT, psi00 for neither, psi11 for both and 0 for a DLT without response. The utility of a dose, divided by 100, has a beta posterior under the quasi-binomial model with the prior utility_prior, and the desirability is its posterior probability of exceeding u_benchmark / 100. The score ranks the desirability among the admissible outcomes of the table, from 1 for the lowest, equal desirabilities sharing the lowest rank. A dose is inadmissible ("E" in the printed table) when the posterior probability, under a uniform prior, that its DLT rate exceeds target is at least cutoff_eli, or that its response rate is below target_resp is at least cutoff_eli_resp. During a trial only the order of the desirabilities of the doses compared matters, so the score gives the same decisions.

References

Lin, R., Zhou, Y., Yan, F., Li, D. and Yuan, Y. (2020). BOIN12: Bayesian optimal interval phase I/II trial design for utility-based dose finding in immunotherapy and targeted therapies. JCO Precision Oncology, 4, 1393-1402. doi:10.1200/PO.20.00257

See also

boin12_simulate, sim_boin12

Examples

# Table 3 of Lin et al. (2020)
tab <- boin12_decision_table(target = 0.35, target_resp = 0.25)
tab
